newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: IATA urges caution over cheap flight offers.
newsitem.headline: IATA urges caution over cheap flight offers.

text.p: The world airlines body IATA warned cheap air fare hunters on Monday they could run into "a lot of grief" if they were found using stolen or forged tickets.
It urged travellers to buy tickets direct from the airlines or from agents approved by IATA, the 253-member International Air Transport Association.
Passengers buying tickets from other sources should establish which airline was to carry them and the number of the ticket and check with the airline before parting with any money, IATA said.
"These simple precautions can save a lot of grief later on," it added in a statement issued to coincide with the busy year-end holiday travel season around the globe.
IATA said the approximately $100 billion a year in revenue the industry generated from selling nearly 400 million international scheduled tickets inevitably attracted criminals.
These focused on theft or forgery of tickets for sale to unwitting travellers seeking to fly at cut rates.
"And so a search for the ultimate bargain can make consumers victims of crime and victims of airlines' attempts to prevent crime," IATA said.

Recent cases in several countries, including Switzerland, "involved consumers in the loss of their money, the need to buy replacement tickets and uncomfortable questioning from both airlines and police," the statement added without giving details.
